feature_contract.goal: Remove the repeated R32 diagnostic window clearing on every ordinary telemetry-disabled D3D9 Present while still resetting the entire sampled p95/p99 frame epoch on toggles, mid-Present changes and game Reset.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: R32 CPU diagnostic counter lifecycle only; no actual game draw, stereo eye resource, camera/RT, HUD, ESC, F11, FFB or DX11/DXVK/Localization changes.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Observed Quest3 capture reported as many as 3298 draws per frame and 11.876 ms game render p95; source proved unconditional writes to frame/window/baseline and global diagnostics every inactive Present, with no dependency on GPU drawing. This removes that redundant CPU work but does not claim measured FPS improvement.
trace_stages: OutRun D3D9 gameplay Draw events optionally publish per-frame counters through R33 workload diagnostics.
R32 Present samples telemetry and records CPU QPC frame/present timing and worst-frame spikes in thread-local windows.
Five-second diagnostic reporting is opt-in, while the headset compositor consumes unchanged original stereo eye resources and GPU submission.
subcomponents: Track diagnostic sampling ownership with thread-local active state and clear counters only on active-to-disabled transitions or partially sampled draw workloads.
Invalidate pending diagnostic windows on mid-Present telemetry-off transitions and D3D9 Reset, preserving eventual 5-second p95/p99 spike logging.
Add numeric 22,000-frame opt-out/toggle/reset model and scoped destructive C++ source regression checks to existing DX9Ex Active policy CI.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Repeated disabled game Presents do not clear the frame, window, baseline and diagnostics cache after the first transition.
Midframe partial draw observation and mid-Present diagnostic change discard the entire stale epoch; Reset clears ownership and original rendering unchanged.
Focused mutation and numeric regression guards plus exact-SHA DX9Ex Active Win32 game/host/package, Domain Isolation, and source impact gates all succeed.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Source R32WithPresentTelemetry branch sampled no telemetry yet every game Present unconditionally assigned five large diagnostic accumulators to zero; Quest3 profiler data confirms frequent Present delivery and costly render path, not that this particular optimization improves FPS.
source_trace: R33 hook forwards each original game Present and optional per-Draw telemetry to R32.
R32WithPresentTelemetry samples diagnostics once and either finalizes or enters unconditional reset of frame/window counters.
Win32 host and Quest3 compositor display unchanged GPU eye images, while 5-second logs report only enabled diagnostic epochs.
diagnosis.root_cause: R32 lacked an epoch-active guard on the disabled Present branch, repeating thread-local/global memory writes already performed on previous inactive frames.
alternatives_rejected: Never drop the first enabled-to-disabled clear: old peaks could leak into the next report.
Never ignore partial-frame draws with no sampled Present: they must be discarded when telemetry goes inactive.
No GPU quality/scaling changes or blanket disabling of telemetry: protect diagnosis of actual 300ms spikes.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: R32PerfWindowActive marks real sampled Present ownership; disabled case zeroes only after an active sampled window or nonempty abandoned workload; Reset and mid-Present disable invalidate the full window.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: New source owner/mutation verifier and 22k disabled Present numeric model, integrated into policy workflow.
diagnosis.repair_evidence: Exact run 38493712709 failed in policy: verify_vr_r31_r32_telemetry_hotpath.py mutation 4 could no longer match R32 disabled Present after transition-only opt-out; mutation 5 also retained a stale Finalize anchor. Validation-bearing daba4bb4 corrects both and verifies Present/Finalize epoch clearing with six live negative mutations. Policy and subsequent Win32 stages passed.
